title: Upstairs mathematics

words.hook: An adult considers a jar of candies beside an ≈20 estimate card. English cognate: estimation; the guess still needs counting.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'estimation', said ehs-tee-mah-SYOHN: an owl gives an ESTIMATE of the candies in a jar, eyes narrowed.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: Two equal bread halves beside 1/2, with the adult presenting them. English cognate: fraction.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'fraction', said frahk-SYOHN: a pizza cut into FRACTIONS, and a dog eyeing the biggest slice.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: A single allocated picnic portion: roll, apple and carrot on one tray. English cognate: ration; not ratio.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'ration', said rah-SYOHN: a RATION of one carrot each for the rabbits, measured with a ruler.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: Five cubes split into three on a mat and two removed, beside 5−2=3; whole display stool included. Direct arithmetic depiction, English subtraction helps recall.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'subtraction', said soos-trahk-SYOHN: SUBTRACTION: ten apples minus three, and a horse munches the missing ones.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: A calculation notebook: 4×3=12. English mathematical: the adjective describes the calculation.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'mathematical', said mah-tay-mah-TEEK: a MATHEMATICAL bee counts the sides of every honeycomb cell.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: An adult holds a quartered disk with one blue quarter beside 25%. English percentage cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'percentage', said poor-sahn-TAHZH: a PERCENTAGE chart where 90 percent of the pie belongs to the cat.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: A complete board and stand show x+2=5, x=3. English equation cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'equation', said ay-kwah-SYOHN: an EQUATION on the board: one cat plus one box equals happiness.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: The complete board and stand carry a bracketed 2×2 mathematical matrix with rows 1,2 and 3,4. English matrix cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'matrix', said mah-TREES: MA plants her TREES in a perfect grid of rows and columns: a living MATRIX.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: A terrestrial globe, equator arrow, crank and complete pedestal show rotation about an axis. English rotation cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'rotation', said roh-tah-SYOHN: a globe in full ROTATION, and a ladybird clinging on.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: Triangle, square and circle frames hang from one complete mobile with bar and ceiling suspension chains. English geometric cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'geometric', said zhay-oh-may-TREEK: a spider weaves a perfect GEOMETRIC triangle web, every side one METER: a neat TRICK.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

words.hook: The adult male mathematician explains with pencil and notebook; his complete seated figure and stool are included. English mathematician cognate.

source_hook.scene: Like English 'mathematician', said mah-tay-mah-tee-SYAN: a MATHEMATICIAN raccoon fills a blackboard with sums and circles one answer.

words.source_note: Adapted to one coherent adult lesson; exact source sense and pronunciation retained.

placement_note: Full meaning-bearing people, props, dedicated apparatus and supports included. Generic upper lesson tables are background furniture rather than mnemonic helpers; visible chairs belong to their people. Foreground display tables/stool and all model stands included. The mathematical notebook’s generic reading-stand pedestal is background support, not part of that cue box. The mobile is ceiling-attached at y=0 by design.
